english: In a population, a disease is present in one person out of every ten. A test for the disease gives a positive result with probability $0.9$ for a person who has the disease and with probability $0.1$ for a person who does not. A person chosen at random from the population is tested twice; given the disease status of the person, the results of the two tests are independent. Let $p_{1}$ be the conditional probability that the person has the disease given that the first test is positive, and let $p_{2}$ be the conditional probability that the person has the disease given that both tests are positive. Then the value of $\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}$ is ______.
hindi: एक जनसंख्या में प्रत्येक दस व्यक्तियों में से एक व्यक्ति को एक रोग है। रोग के लिए एक परीक्षण, रोगी व्यक्ति के लिए प्रायिकता $0.9$ से तथा रोगरहित व्यक्ति के लिए प्रायिकता $0.1$ से धनात्मक परिणाम देता है। जनसंख्या से यादृच्छया चुने गए एक व्यक्ति का दो बार परीक्षण किया जाता है; व्यक्ति की रोग-स्थिति दिए होने पर दोनों परीक्षणों के परिणाम स्वतन्त्र हैं। माना कि $p_{1}$ इसकी सप्रतिबन्ध प्रायिकता है कि व्यक्ति रोगी है जबकि पहला परीक्षण धनात्मक है, तथा $p_{2}$ इसकी सप्रतिबन्ध प्रायिकता है कि व्यक्ति रोगी है जबकि दोनों परीक्षण धनात्मक हैं। तब $\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Let $D$ be 'the person has the disease', $T_{1}$, $T_{2}$ 'first / second test positive'. $P(D)=0.1$, $P(D')=0.9$, $P(T_{i}\mid D)=0.9$, $P(T_{i}\mid D')=0.1$.
One test. Law of total probability: $P(T_{1})=P(D)P(T_{1}\mid D)+P(D')P(T_{1}\mid D')=0.09+0.09=0.18$. Bayes' theorem: $p_{1}=P(D\mid T_{1})=\dfrac{0.09}{0.18}=0.5$.
Two tests. Given $D$, the tests are independent, so $P(T_{1}\cap T_{2}\mid D)=0.9^{2}=0.81$; given $D'$, $P(T_{1}\cap T_{2}\mid D')=0.1^{2}=0.01$.
(Equivalently, the posterior $0.5$ after the first test serves as the prior for the second: $\dfrac{0.5\cdot0.9}{0.5\cdot0.9+0.5\cdot0.1}=0.9$.)
$\dfrac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=\dfrac{0.9}{0.5}=1.8$. Note that the two tests are not unconditionally independent: $P(T_{1}\cap T_{2})=0.09\neq0.18^{2}$.
originality_note: New: one test raises the posterior from 0.1 to 0.5 and a second conditionally independent test to 0.9, and the question compares the two posteriors (way 5: total probability and Bayes applied twice with conditional independence). Closest known: standard single-test diagnostic Bayes problems and sequential Bayes updating in statistics courses. Different because: the second total probability needs conditional, not unconditional, independence, and the trap of squaring P(T1) is built in.

concept_use.Law of total probability: P(T1) = 0.18 and P(T1 n T2) = 0.09 are found by the law of total probability over D and D'.
concept_use.Bayes' theorem: p1 = 0.5 and p2 = 0.9 are posteriors by Bayes' theorem.
